title: Set camshaft timing and verify deviation

notices.text: THE STEP THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE ENGINE LIVES. Bring the engine to TDC cylinder 1 on the compression stroke and lock it there. Fit the cam holding/locking fixtures to both banks (Porsche 9595-series tooling or a competent aftermarket equivalent such as the P253 type). Time the chains, release the tensioners, then rotate the engine through at least two full turns BY HAND — if anything binds, stop and find out why before you apply any more force. Re-check TDC and re-verify the locks still drop in. A widely used belt-and-braces practice among M96 builders is red thread locker on the cam sprocket bolts as insurance against timing slip. Finally, after first start, read camshaft deviation for both banks with a scan tool and compare against the values you logged at the very beginning — that is the closed loop on the whole job.
